name: Sunriver
label: Sunriver
about_prose: Sunriver sits 15 miles south of Bend on the east bank of the Deschutes River, on land that started out as Camp Abbot, a U.S. Army combat engineer training post built in 1942 and torn down by 1944 once the war effort moved on. Developers John Gray and Donald McCallum bought the former Army tract in 1965 and picked the name Sunriver. The first condominiums and the original lodge opened in 1968, Skidmore, Owings and Merrill finished the master plan in 1969, and the Sunriver post office opened that July. The community sits on the grounds of the former Shonquest Ranch.

Roughly 4,200 homesites make up the 3,300-acre plan, split between single-family homes, condominiums, and cabins. The 2020 Census counted 2,023 full-time residents, up from 1,393 in 2010 and 1,393 in 2000, a 45 percent jump in a decade. Most homesites still turn over to guests and second-home owners the rest of the year. A lot of your neighbors will not be around most weeks, and the community's rhythm follows the resort calendar more than a typical residential street would.

The Sunriver Owners Association runs the common areas, the path network, and the design standards for every property in the plan. Membership is automatic once you close, no opting out. Any exterior change, from a repainted fascia board to removing a native tree, needs Design Committee approval before you order the materials, and the association runs annual inspections for fire-hazard brush and noxious weeds. Sunriver Resort is a separate entity. It runs the hotel, the golf courses, the spa, the marina, and the stables. Buying here means answering to two organizations instead of one, and giving up some of the exterior freedom a non-HOA lot would give you.

The paved path network runs 34 miles, separated from the roads, including a 12-mile round trip on the Sun Lava Path out to Benham Falls and the Lava Lands Visitor Center in the Newberry National Volcanic Monument. Three golf courses share the property. Crosswater is the private one, a 600-acre heathland-style course designed by Robert E. Cupp and opened in 1995, ranked among Golf Digest's 100 Greatest. The Woodlands, designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr., opened in 1982. The Meadows opened in 1969 and was redesigned by John Fought in 1999. SHARC, the 22-acre aquatic and recreation center, adds a lazy river in summer and a snow-tubing hill in winter. The Sunriver Nature Center and Observatory, an eight-acre campus dating to 1968, holds the largest publicly accessible telescope collection in the country, and the community earned an official Dark Sky designation in 2020.

Families with school-age kids feed into Bend-La Pine Schools. Three Rivers School, inside Sunriver, covers kindergarten through eighth grade. There is no high school in the community itself. Students choose Caldera or La Pine starting in ninth grade, which means a bus ride or a daily drive once your kids reach that age.

Bend's Old Mill District is a 25-minute drive north on US-97, Redmond Airport is 41 minutes, and Mt. Bachelor is 30 minutes up the Cascade Lakes Highway. Sunriver also runs its own general aviation airport, privately owned by Sunriver Resort, with a 5,455-foot runway and parking for up to 170 aircraft. It draws a segment of buyer a typical Central Oregon subdivision does not: people who fly themselves in and out.

Day to day errands stay small. The Sunriver Country Store in the Village and the Sunriver Marketplace at the north entrance both carry groceries, a deli, and daily essentials, but neither is a full supermarket. Locals on the community's own discussion boards put the in-plan selection at roughly half of what you would find at a Bend grocery chain, which is why most residents still make regular trips north for a full shop. Winters run cold at 4,170 feet of elevation. Even with more than 300 sunny days most years, the recorded low here is negative 27 degrees Fahrenheit, and the same roads that sit quiet in November fill with float traffic and bike traffic on a July weekend. Sunriver runs on a resort's calendar, not a small town's. That suits a buyer who wants the swing between empty and crowded. It will frustrate someone looking for the same pace every month of the year.

amenities.name: Crosswater Club
amenities.description: A 600-acre heathland-style course by Robert E. Cupp, opened 1995. The Deschutes and Little Deschutes rivers come into play on several holes. Ranked among Golf Digest's 100 Greatest Courses.
amenities.access: Members and Sunriver Resort guests only

amenities.name: Woodlands Course
amenities.description: 18-hole course by Robert Trent Jones Jr., opened 1982. Par 72, 6,847 yards, slope 143.
amenities.access: Resort guests and public tee times

amenities.name: Meadows Course
amenities.description: 18-hole course opened 1969, redesigned by John Fought in 1999. Par 71, 7,012 yards, slope 140.
amenities.access: Resort guests and public tee times

amenities.name: SHARC Aquatic and Recreation Center
amenities.description: A 22-acre facility with a seasonal lazy river, water slides, a tot pool, a year-round snow-tubing hill, disc golf, and event space.

amenities.name: Paved Path Network
amenities.description: 34 miles of paved paths separated from roads, plus a 12-mile round-trip Sun Lava Path to Benham Falls and the Lava Lands Visitor Center.

amenities.name: Sunriver Marina
amenities.description: Deschutes River marina renting canoes, kayaks, paddleboards, tubes, and rafts, with shuttle service for a 6-mile float.

amenities.name: Sunriver Stables
amenities.description: Guided trail rides through pine forest, seasonally mid-April through September, with pony rides available.

amenities.name: The Cove Aquatic Center
amenities.description: 10,000-square-foot indoor facility with a heated pool, lazy river, two-story waterslide, splash pad, and outdoor spas.

amenities.name: Sunriver Nature Center and Observatory
amenities.description: An eight-acre campus established in 1968. The observatory holds the largest publicly accessible telescope collection in the United States. Sunriver earned a Dark Sky designation in 2020.

amenities.name: The Village at Sunriver
amenities.description: A commercial district of locally owned restaurants and shops, including Sunriver Brewing Company.

course_specs.summary: Five courses: Crosswater (1995, Robert E. Cupp, private/resort-guest, Golf Digest Top 100), Woodlands (1982, Robert Trent Jones Jr., par 72, 6,847 yds), Meadows (1969, redesigned by John Fought 1999, par 71, 7,012 yds), plus the shorter family courses Caldera Links and Gray's Trail.
